\section[gajaḥ]{\sk{गजः} (gajaḥ) — an elephant}

\label{lesson:SA-C79-elephant}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for flatbread, then the Sanskrit for sweet rice pudding.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{गजः}}
\textbf{\sk{गजः}} (\emph{gajaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}an elephant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The biggest animal on land.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gajaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gajaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{gajaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for flatbread, then the Sanskrit for sweet rice pudding, then say \emph{gajaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{गजः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An elephant\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
